blocks.section: Parātrīśikāvivaraṇa
blocks.text: Abhinavagupta has spent seventeen installments turning the Sanskrit alphabet into the living body of Śakti. Now he discovers a rather inconvenient problem: somebody had to decide what the words mean. He interrogates the meaning of “cow,” summons Utpaladeva, catches linguistic convention in a philosophical infinite regress, and finally brings the entire bloody dictionary back to Anuttara, Bindu and Visarga.

blocks.text: Now we can finally answer the question that began this installment.

blocks.text: Who decided that go means cow?
blocks.directed: Who decided that go means cow?

blocks.section: 26. The final insight - The meaning of “cow” doesn't create
blocks.text: But Abhinavagupta asks a deeper question.
blocks.directed: But Abhinavagupta asks a deeper question.

blocks.section: 26. The final insight - The meaning of “cow” doesn't create
blocks.text: What makes it possible for a conscious being to learn and use such a convention?
blocks.directed: What makes it possible for a conscious being to learn and use such a convention?

blocks.section: 26. The final insight - The meaning of “cow” doesn't create
blocks.text: How can the word be apprehended?

blocks.section: 26. The final insight - The meaning of “cow” doesn't create

blocks.section: 26. The final insight - The meaning of “cow” doesn't create

blocks.section: 26. The final insight - The meaning of “cow” doesn't create
blocks.text: How can the original agreement be understood if every act of understanding requires an earlier agreement?

blocks.section: 26. The final insight - The meaning of “cow” doesn't create
blocks.text: His answer is that convention presupposes a more fundamental capacity of consciousness.
blocks.directed: His answer is that convention presupposes a more fundamental capacity of consciousness.

blocks.section: 26. The final insight - The meaning of “cow” doesn't create
blocks.text: And in Trika, that capacity ultimately belongs to the supreme self-revealing reality.
blocks.directed: And in Trika, that capacity ultimately belongs to the supreme self-revealing reality.

blocks.section: 26. The final insight - The meaning of “cow” doesn't create
blocks.text: The word doesn't create the awareness that understands it.
blocks.directed: The word doesn't create the awareness that understands it.

blocks.section: 26. The final insight - The meaning of “cow” doesn't create
blocks.text: The awareness makes the meaningful use of the word possible.
blocks.directed: The awareness makes the meaningful use of the word possible.

blocks.section: 26. The final insight - The meaning of “cow” doesn't create
blocks.text: Now this doesn't mean the conventional meaning of go is innate.
blocks.directed: Now this doesn't mean the conventional meaning of go is innate.

blocks.section: 26. The final insight - The meaning of “cow” doesn't create
blocks.text: Nor that Sanskrit is the only possible language.
blocks.directed: Nor that Sanskrit is the only possible language.

blocks.section: 26. The final insight - The meaning of “cow” doesn't create
blocks.text: Nor that every animal cry is secretly a grammatically complete Sanskrit sentence.
blocks.directed: Nor that every animal cry is secretly a grammatically complete Sanskrit sentence.

blocks.section: 26. The final insight - The meaning of “cow” doesn't create
blocks.text: It means that the capacity for conscious apprehension cannot be exhaustively reduced to the conventions formed within it.
blocks.directed: It means that the capacity for conscious apprehension cannot be exhaustively reduced to the conventions formed within it.

blocks.section: 26. The final insight - The meaning of “cow” doesn't create
blocks.text: And that's a genuinely profound distinction.
blocks.directed: And that's a genuinely profound distinction.

blocks.section: 26. The final insight - The meaning of “cow” doesn't create
blocks.text: Because it changes how we understand the relationship between sacred speech and realization.
blocks.directed: Because it changes how we understand the relationship between sacred speech and realization.

blocks.section: 26. The final insight - The meaning of “cow” doesn't create
blocks.text: The word Śiva isn't the supreme reality merely because somebody has written four Sanskrit letters.
blocks.directed: The word Śiva isn't the supreme reality merely because somebody has written four Sanskrit letters.

blocks.section: 26. The final insight - The meaning of “cow” doesn't create
blocks.text: The word vimarśa doesn't manufacture self-awareness.
blocks.directed: The word vimarśa doesn't manufacture self-awareness.

blocks.section: 26. The final insight - The meaning of “cow” doesn't create
blocks.text: And memorizing the definition of Anuttara doesn't create the unsurpassable conscious ground.
blocks.directed: And memorizing the definition of Anuttara doesn't create the unsurpassable conscious ground.

blocks.section: 26. The final insight - The meaning of “cow” doesn't create
blocks.text: Those words can serve as means of understanding.
blocks.directed: Those words can serve as means of understanding.

blocks.section: 26. The final insight - The meaning of “cow” doesn't create
blocks.text: But the conscious reality through which they're understood is the very subject of the teaching.
blocks.directed: But the conscious reality through which they're understood is the very subject of the teaching.

blocks.section: 26. The final insight - The meaning of “cow” doesn't create
blocks.text: The teaching points through language toward the nature of awareness itself.
blocks.directed: The teaching points through language toward the nature of awareness itself.

blocks.section: 26. The final insight - The meaning of “cow” doesn't create
blocks.text: And now Abhinavagupta completes the circle.
blocks.directed: And now Abhinavagupta completes the circle.

blocks.section: 26. The final insight - The meaning of “cow” doesn't create
